inputs.original_text: The real issue isn’t that renters have too many protections; it’s that families are still facing eviction and emergency accommodation while secure housing remains out of reach. Six-year leases from March 1 should be judged by whether they give tenants more stability, not dismissed because they might inconvenience landlords. Pointing to tenancy figures means little if people still cannot count on keeping a home. The government needs to put secure, affordable homes ahead of protecting the market’s convenience—and stop treating housing insecurity as a problem renters should simply navigate.
inputs.modified_text: The housing debate keeps getting turned into a question of whether landlords might be inconvenienced, while families face eviction and emergency accommodation. Six-year leases from March 1 should be judged by whether they give renters real security—not by whether they preserve the market’s comfort. Tenancy figures mean little when people still can’t rely on keeping a home. Government should prioritize secure, affordable housing and stop making renters bear the consequences of a system that leaves housing out of reach.
